newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Products-Gasoline diffs firm, NYMEX slides.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Products-Gasoline diffs firm, NYMEX slides.

text.p: Spot refined products prices fell sharply Friday as the NYMEX basis prices headed south throughout the day.
However, some gasoline differentials firmed by late in the day in modest activity, traders said.

The NYMEX extended its recent bearish movement and pressuring outright products' prices. July gasoline fell 2.69 cents to settle at 57.13 cents a gallon, while July heating oil dropped 1.80 cents to finish at 51.52 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF COAST
Conventional unleaded gasoline differentials retained their firmer levels into the afternoon as refiners continued to line up supply for a shipping dealine on the Colonial Pipeline.

"The market is fairly well supplied, so it's not a necessity to buy. But, people want to make sure they are covered (for the deadline)," said a U.S. Gulf trader, noting the stronger differentials are purely linked to the shipping deadline and not supply fundamentals.
Prompt conventional unleaded M1 gasoline was offered at 0.75 cent under NYMEX July gasoline, gaining a 0.25 cent over Thursday's levels.

Prompt heating oil was traded at 2.15 cents under NYMEX July heat, within the price range of 2.05 to 2.30 cents talked on Thursday. Heating oil futures prices are becoming more indicative of spot supply, preventing the difference to the spot prices from widening, dealers said.
NYMEX July heating oil fell 4.45 cents a gallon for the week.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Harbor differentials showed little movement Friday, though some weakness was noted in the prompt regular conventional M2 gasoline, traders said.
Prompt conventional M2 was talked near 2.35 cents under the July NYMEX gasoline, traders said, though thin market conditions made it hard to pin down price levels.
Prompt reformulated A2 gasoline was talked between 0.10 and 0.35 cent over the July NYMEX, slightly up from late Thursday levels.
Premium grade reformulated V2 gasoline was seen between about 4.00 and 4.25 cents over the July futures, also up from Thursday's levels.
MIDCONTINENT

Midcontinent product markets, shell-shocked by the sharp gasoline-led downturn on NYMEX, were virtually dormant Friday afternoon, with the only deals on barrels for deferred delivery that were beyond the worst of the NYMEX turbulence.

"It's ostrich day in the Midwest when the market does this," said one trader referring not only to the lack of liquidity Friday but also the fact that many traders actually left their offices when the NYMEX vortex started to suck prices downward.
Still the Group Three market, where differential movement as a rule tends to be a bit more volatile than in the Chicago market, showed signs of moving up at least notionally in response to the NYMEX.
Prompt unleaded in the Group got done in the early going at 4.75 cents over July unleaded futures, and was rumored to have been done at 5.00 cents over by the time the NYMEX closed.
Also bids on Group X-grade low sulphur diesel crept up 0.25 cent to 4.25 cent over July NYMEX, with offers notionally pegged at 4.75 cents over.
Ratable July X-Grade barrels were heard done at 1.67 cents over NYMEX August futures.
Looking ahead as the dust settles from the NYMEX selloff, traders expect the Chicago market to shed Friday's staidness in favor of a response, differentially speaking.

While many traders expect differentials to firm to equalize NYMEX losses, concerns about high refinery run rates and the consequent buildup of stocks in the midcontinent has created some sense among traders that differentials might also be talked lower in the coming week.
